source: Modeled: Sweden income deciles (SSB/SCB) x Finland necessity-share curve (Statistics Finland HBS 2022)
methodology: Sweden's household budget/consumption survey was discontinued (Norway: Forbruksundersokelsen, after 2012; Sweden: HUT, after 2009), so no post-discontinuation category-level expenditure data exists. Per docs/v3-plan.md's peer-modeling guidance, we model Sweden's necessity/discretionary expenditure split by: (1) computing Finland's (Statistics Finland Household Budget Survey / Kulutustutkimus 2022, the most recent Nordic HBS with full category-level detail) necessity share [minimal strictness: housing + food_at_home + healthcare_oop + transport_work-or-0.6x(transport_total)] as a fraction of total household expenditure, separately for each of Finland's 5 income quintiles; (2) fitting a monotone piecewise-linear interpolation of this necessity-share curve across quintile centers (mapped to decile positions 1.5, 3.5, 5.5, 7.5, 9.5), holding the share constant at Finland's q1 value below the curve's lower anchor and at Finland's q5 value above its upper anchor (per v3-plan.md's stated extrapolation rule); (3) applying the resulting decile-indexed necessity-share curve directly to Sweden's own published income-decile disposable-income figures (source: SCB HE0110F/TabVX10InkStrukt). SIMPLIFYING ASSUMPTION (flagged, not hidden): because Sweden publishes income but not expenditure totals, we assume total household expenditure approximately equals disposable income at each decile (i.e., a 0% net saving rate) purely for the purpose of allocating the necessity/discretionary split -- this will understate the true expenditure total if Sweden households save a meaningfully positive share of disposable income at a given decile (true almost everywhere, especially at high deciles), so 'necessity_total_modeled' should be read as a share-of-income lower bound / a conservative necessity floor rather than a literal expenditure prediction. Frontend should badge this data 'Modeled from FI peer (Tier C)' per v3-plan.md, with caveat text: "Sweden's household budget survey was discontinued after 2009. Necessity floor here assumes Swedish households allocate spending in similar proportions to Finnish households at the same income level."
